content:
Hi everyone,

we've coordinated with @Joseph Tooby-Smith to build a new version of the website https://physlib.io. @Gabriele Battimelli did the heavy lifting

Here it is: https://physlib-website.vercel.app

We'd appreciate any feedback on it! Also, since this has come up in a couple of chats, I just want to reassure people we'll keep the code fully open source and maintain it in a way that serves the community. Courtesy of our clients at Kernel Science :slight_smile:

Once we're done with this round of feedbacks we'll put it under the current domain: https://physlib.io
The fixed toolbar at the top probably warrants an opaque background.

A few link/attribution bugs to fix before pointing physlib.io here:

  1. GitHub links point to the old repo. "View on GitHub" (hero), nav "GitHub", footer "GitHub ↗", and the footer attribution all link to github.com/lean-phys-community/PhysLean. Should be github.com/leanprover-community/physlib. GitHub's auto-redirect masks this for now, but the links are stale.
  2. Footer says "Maintained by the lean-phys-community" — should be leanprover-community post-move.
  3. "Curated Notes ↗" → notes.physlean.com is a dead link (DNS does not resolve). Either remove it or repoint.
  4. Zulip links use 479953-PhysLean ("Discussion ↗", "Join Community"). Functionally OK (Zulip routes by channel ID) but the channel was renamed to Physlib.
Link to Curated Notes should be removed entirely here - page no longer exists.

Hi Kim,

Thanks for the detailed feedback! I’ve just finished pushing those updates to the project:
Fixed Toolbar: The top navigation bar now has a fully opaque background to improve legibility against the page content.
GitHub Migration: All repository links (Hero CTA, Nav, Footer, and Attribution) have been updated from lean-phys-community/PhysLean to leanprover-community/physlib.
Community Attribution: The footer attribution now correctly identifies the project as maintained by the leanprover-community.
Curated Notes: Since the link was dead, I have removed it from the navigation, footer, and the "Get Involved" page.
Zulip Links: All discussion links have been updated to reference the renamed #physlib channel.

Let me know if there’s anything else you’d like me to tweak!

Best,
Gabriele
Unless anyone objects, I can port https://physlib.io over on Friday.
I don’t think the sidebar appears on eg the TODO page on a mobile (the one with the links to all the other pages) - also not clear how you get those links on a mobile.
Good catch on the mobile navigation! I’ve just pushed an update to fix this.

(https version of the website of physlib.io is down temporarily, while we do this change - http version is still up, you might (and should hopefully) get a privacy warning when trying to connect to the site)
Website now totally live. Many thanks @Gabriele Battimelli and @Fabio Anzà !
@Fabio Anzà & @Gabriele Battimelli if one wants to make a change to the website how is the best way to do it? Is there a GitHub repo?
It was on @Gabriele Battimelli private GitHub. He is now moving it inside Kernel Science organization and we'll make sure it auto-pushes into Vercel. We'll do things the usual way, via pull requests

Here we go: https://github.com/Kernel-Science/physlib-website

@Joseph Tooby-Smith please do a light PR (some very simple change) before doing the changes you wanted to do, so we can test if the automation works properly
Made a trivial PR.
Hi Joseph, I just merged your PR and it instantly triggered a redeployment on vercel :)

The feature I am wanting to add (though may not have the time to do so) is: It would be nice to be able to write specifically structured GitHub issues on the Physlib repo which get added to the TODO list.

Hey Joseph! I went ahead and implemented that feature. Any open GitHub issue on the Physlib repo will automatically appear in the TODO list on the website. Issues show up under the "TODO Items" filter with a "GitHub Issue" badge to distinguish them from the Lean-generated ones. The list refreshes twice a day alongside the existing doc build.

@Gabriele Battimelli Many thanks! Is there any specific format the GitHub issues need to take for it to appear in the list? A quick look at the TODO list now doesn't show any (though I guess things might not have updated).
Hi Jospeh, yess i saw the github action run proprely but vercel didn't fetch the data from extracted the github issues. Everything is working now

For the TODO list, I was wondering if we could put a message which says when it was last updated. I think this would make it easy for people to see that it 1) is up to date, and 2) is still working correctly.
Hi Joseph, I just added this to the TODO List
Great! Many thanks Gabriele.
Hey @Gabriele Battimelli and @Fabio Anzà, do you know if the website is updating? The TODO list hasn't updated since July. Also I just merged one of @Alex Zughaid 's PRs
Hey Joseph, you were right. Vercel's free plan was blocking commits not authored by me. I found a workaround by updating the author names on the deploy hook, so it should work smoothly from now on.
Hi guys, a few of my PRs were merged this morning but the changes have not gone live yet. The build works on my local machine but im wondering if something else has broken.
Hi Alex, I got the Vercel notification this morning. Looking into it now to see if it's a configuration issue on Vercel or something in the codebase like missing dependencies.
It was a small bug in download-docs.js, It should work from now on
Thanks!

Is this the correct place to mention this issue ?

The link for website_repo goes to a 404 Page Not Found.
https://physlib.io/project-ideas
Thanks for pointing this out! If you did not find it the Github is https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib
Thank you for pointing that out. I’ll look into it right now
It’s fixed now. Thank you @Daniel Morrison !
